introH2: 🏝️ What kind of stays does Koh Tao in Surat Thani have, and how do you pick the right one for your trip?
introHtml: Koh Tao is a small island in the Gulf of Thailand, in the Surat Thani province, known as Thailand's diving mecca — one of the places that certifies the most new divers anywhere in the world, with a chilled mood that's more about relaxing and diving than glossy partying · what many don't realise is that most of the island's stays are bungalows and dive resorts on a modest budget, with only a scattering of luxury resorts · Koh Tao is reached by catamaran (Lomprayah/Songserm) from Chumphon (~1.5–2 hrs), Surat Thani, Koh Samui or Koh Phangan, arriving at Mae Haad pier, from where you take a songthaew/taxi/boat to your beach · the main beaches run roughly like this — Sairee Beach is the long, buzzing main strip with plenty of shops, bars and dive schools · Chalok Baan Kao to the south is quieter · Mae Haad (the pier/village) is easy to walk around · Tanote Bay has the prettiest snorkelling but is remote · Haad Tien/Shark Bay is the most private · we've ranked this list by real guest review scores, rounding up 8 stays we've reviewed in depth, giving both the good points and the honest caveats, comparing prices across 3 sites with direct booking links for each.
mrtHtml: Koh Tao is reached by catamaran (Lomprayah/Songserm) from Chumphon (~1.5–2 hrs), Surat Thani, Koh Samui or Koh Phangan, arriving at Mae Haad pier, from where you take a songthaew/taxi/boat to your beach · the main beaches: Sairee Beach the long, buzzing main strip with plenty of shops, bars and dive schools · Chalok Baan Kao in the south, quieter · Mae Haad the pier/village, easy to walk around · Tanote Bay the prettiest snorkelling, but remote · Haad Tien/Shark Bay the most private · the remote bays need a boat/car transfer · ⚠️ in the monsoon season (Oct–Dec) rough seas can cancel the boats, so always check before you travel.

entries.storyHtml: If you've ever heard that Tanote Bay is one of the prettiest snorkelling spots on Koh Tao, Mountain Reef Beach Resort is the main resort planted right on it · it's a quiet, remote east-coast bay with no town to stroll like Sairee Beach, and the draw is that swimming just a few metres off the sand puts you over healthy coral, shoals of fish and sometimes sea turtles · there are both waterfront rock-side bungalows and affordable fan huts up the forested slope, starting around ฿1,100/night with a score of 8.3 · the honest caveats: the cheapest rooms are simple fan huts up the hill that you have to climb to, it's remote so you'll be taking a taxi across the island, and the choice of restaurants around the bay is thin.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: if you're coming mainly to snorkel, pick a Family Room Beachfront or a rock-side bungalow a few steps from the water, while the thrifty who can live with a fan pick the Fan Hillside Hut · bring your own snorkel gear, and budget for a taxi across the island since Tanote Bay is far from the pier.

adviceTitle: How do you pick a Koh Tao stay that fits your trip?

advice.head: Coming to learn to dive/dive mainly, want a buzzing beachfront stay
advice.bodyHtml: → Ban's Diving Resort ฿700, a legendary PADI 5-Star dive-training base right on Sairee Beach, often with combined room + course deals · or Sairee Cottage Resort ฿700, a beachfront bungalow in the heart of the strip with an in-house PADI 5-Star dive centre, the best value on the list · both are on buzzing Sairee Beach, an easy walk to shops and bars

advice.head: Want luxury/a pool villa for a special celebration
advice.bodyHtml: → Koh Tao Heights Pool Villas ฿5,500, private pool villas with Koh Nang Yuan views on the North Sairee hillside, good for couples · or Jamahkiri Dive Resort & Spa ฿3,500, a 5-star Balinese-style clifftop resort at Shark Bay with an in-house spa and dive centre · both are remote and on a slope, so use the shuttle

advice.head: Want a quiet bay with snorkelling over coral off the sand
advice.bodyHtml: → Mountain Reef Beach Resort ฿1,100, on Tanote Bay, one of the prettiest snorkelling spots on the island, coral right off the sand · or Haadtien Beach Resort ฿3,200, villas at Ao Thian Ok (Shark Bay), a private white beach 380 metres long with snorkelling in front of your room · both are remote, so budget for taxis/meals at the resort

advice.head: Want a quiet boutique, not focused on diving/partying
advice.bodyHtml: → Chintakiri Resort ฿1,900, a boutique hillside bungalow with sea views at Chalok Baan Kao, quiet and calm · or Sensi Paradise Beach Resort ฿2,900, wooden garden bungalows on Mae Haad beach, within walking distance of the pier and village, good for anyone who doesn't want to rent a vehicle

faqTitle: FAQ — questions travellers often ask about staying on Koh Tao, Surat Thani

faq.q: ❓ How do you get to Koh Tao, do you have to take a boat?
faq.a: Koh Tao has no airport, so you go by boat · take a catamaran (Lomprayah / Songserm) from Chumphon, about 1.5–2 hrs, the fastest and most popular route, or from Surat Thani, Koh Samui and Koh Phangan, all arriving at Mae Haad pier · from Mae Haad take a songthaew/taxi/water taxi to your beach · coming from Bangkok, people usually take the train or a coach down to Chumphon then the boat, or fly to Samui/Surat Thani and connect by boat

faq.q: ❓ Which beach on Koh Tao should I stay at, buzzing Sairee vs a quiet bay?
faq.a: It depends on your style · Sairee Beach is the long, busiest main strip, restaurants, bars and dive shops lined up by the dozen, good for people who like to stroll around, lively and learn to dive, like Sairee Cottage and Ban's Diving · Chalok, Mae Haad, Tanote Bay and Haad Tien/Shark Bay are quieter and more private, good for couples and relaxers, like Chintakiri, Sensi Paradise, Mountain Reef, Jamahkiri and Haadtien · the remote bays need a boat/car transfer, so allow for the travel

faq.q: ❓ Do you have to be able to dive to stay on Koh Tao, is it worth it without diving?
faq.a: Not at all · although Koh Tao is a divers' island, many of the stays on this list suit non-divers too · Koh Tao Heights (pool villas with lovely views), Chintakiri (a quiet hillside boutique) and Sensi Paradise (garden bungalows by the village) are more about relaxing than diving · non-divers still enjoy snorkelling off the sand at Tanote Bay and Shark Bay, boat trips around the island to Koh Nang Yuan, or just chilling on the beach for the sunset

faq.q: ❓ When is the best time for Koh Tao, do the boats really stop in the monsoon?
faq.a: The finest weather is February–April, clear seas, small waves, the best time for diving, but prices are high and rooms fill fast · during the monsoon season, October–December, there are strong waves and lots of rain, and the catamaran can be cancelled on some days, which can leave you stuck on or off the island against your plan, so check the ferry schedule and allow spare days · the rest of the year the weather is good with rain in spells and is still fine for travel · always check the weather and ferry schedule before you go

faq.q: ❓ Does Koh Tao have luxury stays, or only light-budget bungalows?
faq.a: It has both, but most are bungalows and dive resorts on a modest budget — starting at just ฿700, like Sairee Cottage and Ban's Diving on Sairee Beach · the luxury side is a scattering, like Koh Tao Heights Pool Villas ฿5,500 (private pool villas) and Jamahkiri Dive Resort & Spa ฿3,500 (5-star on the cliff at Shark Bay) · the mid-range includes Chintakiri, Sensi Paradise and Haadtien · choose by budget and check the real reviews before booking
